context.title: The Battle Is God's
context.summary: Facing a huge invasion, Jehoshaphat calls a fast and prays. A Levite prophesies that the battle is God's. Singers lead the army out, and the enemies destroy one another.
context.background: The invaders came around the Dead Sea to En-gedi (v. 2), an oasis on its western shore, within striking distance of Jerusalem. Jahaziel, who prophesies, is a Levite descended from Asaph the musician (v. 14). The 'valley of Berachah' (v. 26) means 'valley of blessing.'

customs.note: Going without food as a sign of urgent dependence on God in a crisis.

watchFor: 'Neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee' (v. 12).
'Stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD' echoes Moses at the Red Sea (v. 17).

w: and just as had finished they

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: The son and successor of Asa, king of Judah. After fortifying his kingdom against Israel (2 Chr. 17:1, 2), he set himself to cleanse the land of idolatry (1 Kings 22:43).

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

people.name: Jahaziel
people.summary: The son of Zechariah, a Levite of the family of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14-17).

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: A Levite of the sons of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14).

people.name: Azubah
people.summary: The daughter of Shilhi, and mother of king Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42).

people.name: Asa
people.summary: Physician, son of Abijah and grandson of Rehoboam, was the third king of Judah. He was zealous in maintaining the true worship of God, and in rooting all idolatry, with its accompanying immoralities, out of the land (1 Kings 15:8-14).

people.name: Hanani
people.summary: A prophet who was sent to rebuke king Asa for entering into a league with Benhadad I., king of Syria, against Judah (2 Chr. 16:1-10).

people.name: Jehu
people.summary: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah (1 Kings 16:1, 7; 2 Chr. 19:2; 20:34), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

people.name: Ahaziah
people.summary: The son and successor of Ahab. He followed the counsels of his mother Jezebel, and imitated in wickedness the ways of his father. In his reign the Moabites revolted from under his authority (2 Kings 3:5-7).

people.name: Eliezer
people.summary: A prophet in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 20:37).

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: Engedi
places.summary: Fountain of the kid, place in the wilderness of Judah (Josh. 15:62), on the western shore of the Dead Sea (Ezek. 47:10), and nearly equidistant from both extremities.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Ammon
places.summary: The usual name of the descendants of Ammon, the son of Lot (Gen. 19:38). From the very beginning (Deut. 2:16-20) of their history till they are lost sight of (Judg. 5:2), this tribe is closely associated with the Moabites (Judg. 10:11; 2 Chr. 20:1; Zeph. 2:8).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Jeruel
places.summary: Founded by God, a “desert” on the ascent from the valley of the Dead Sea towards Jerusalem. It lay beyond the wilderness of Tekoa, in the direction of Engedi (2 Chr. 20:16, 20).

places.name: Ziz
places.summary: Projecting; a flower, a cleft or pass, probably that near En-gedi, which leads up from the Dead Sea (2 Chr. 20:16) in the direction of Tekoa; now Tell Hasasah.

places.name: Tekoa
places.summary: Pitching of tents; fastening down, a town of Judah, about 12 miles south of Jerusalem, and visible from the city. From this place Joab procured a “wise woman,” who pretended to be in great affliction, and skilfully made her case known to David.

places.name: Seir
places.summary: The name of a mountainous region occupied by the Edomites, extending along the eastern side of the Arabah from the south-eastern extremity of the Dead Sea to near the Akabah, or the eastern branch of the Red Sea.

places.name: valley of Beracah
places.summary: A valley not far from Engedi, where Jehoshaphat overthrew the Moabites and Ammonites (2 Chr. 20:26). It has been identified with the valley of Bereikut.

places.name: Ezion-geber
places.summary: The giant’s backbone (so called from the head of a mountain which runs out into the sea), an ancient city and harbour at the north-east end of the Elanitic branch of the Red Sea, the Gulf of Akabah, near Elath or Eloth (Num. 33:35; Deut. 2:8).

places.name: Tarshish
places.summary: The name of a place which first comes into notice in the days of Solomon. The question as to the locality of Tarshish has given rise to not a little discussion.

places.name: Mareshah
places.summary: Possession, a city in the plain of Judah (John. 15:44). Here Asa defeated Zerah the Ethiopian (2 Chr. 14:9, 10).
